text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Mubarak calls on Israel to be flexible so that peace talks with Syria can resume; he tells Israeli television that Syrian President Hafez al-Assad is ready for negotations if they pick up from where the previous round left off. Israeli television says Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is to visit Egypt next week for talks with Mubarak.
- President in talks with president of Niger on African issues and ways to boost trade relations.
- Planning Ministry prepares groundwork for next four five-year plans.
- Egyptian ambassador to the United States says that Mubarak's forthcoming visit to Washington is an indication of the depth of ties between two countries.
- Defence minister tells parliament that armed forces continue to develop their fighting skills.
- Central Bank foreign currency reserves till end of December 1996 up to $19 billion from $18.5 billion till end of June of that year.
- Mubarak in talks with Tataristan president on ways to boost economic ties.
- Former Israeli foreign minister says Mubarak stressed the importance of just and comprehensive peace.
- Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib says there will be a five-year tax exemption for any new extension of current production lines to encourage local production.
- New York stock market to hold workshop on Egyptian stock exchange on March 4.
- Minister of State for the People's Assembly & Shura Assembly Kamal el-Shazli says government will pass law on relation between land owners and land lessee by October.
- Governors' Council to discuss with Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri on Wednesday investment projects in provinces.
- Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation to increase amount it buys from foreign companies in western desert.
